questions.question: Pressure increase from a 2.0 m depth in water (ρ≈1000 kg/m³) is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: About 10 kPa per meter of water; 2 m → ~20 kPa.

questions.question: A 5 cm² piston supports a 12,000 N car using a 400 cm² output piston. Input force needed is:
questions.fastStrategy: Force scales with area ratio; 1/80 of 12,000 ≈ 150.

questions.question: Gauge pressure at 30 m depth in freshwater is about:
questions.explanation: Roughly 1 atm per 10 m of water. 30 m → ~3 atm gauge.

questions.question: Continuity: Water flows in a pipe from 6 cm diameter to 3 cm diameter. Speed increases by factor:
questions.explanation: A ∝ d². Area ratio (6/3)² = 4. To conserve flow, speed quadruples.

questions.question: A 2.5 kg object displaces 2.0 L of water. It will:
questions.explanation: Displaced water weight = ρVg ≈ 1000×0.002×9.8 ≈ 19.6 N. Object weight ≈ 24.5 N. Weight exceeds buoyant → sinks.
questions.fastStrategy: Object heavier than displaced water → sinks.

questions.question: A manometer shows a 18 cm mercury column difference (ρHg≈13,600 kg/m³). Gauge pressure is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: Mercury column ~0.1 m gives ~13 kPa; 0.18 m → ~24 kPa.

questions.question: A 1.5 L container is filled with oil (ρ=800 kg/m³). Its mass is:
A Venturi has pressures 120 kPa (wide) and 90 kPa (narrow). Flow speed in wide section is 4 m/s. Density 1000 kg/m³. Speed in narrow section is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: 30 kPa head ~3 m water → adds ~8 m/s to speed; result ~9 m/s.

questions.question: Flow rate through a 0.5 cm² nozzle at 12 m/s is:
questions.explanation: Area 0.5 cm² = 0.5×1e-4 m² = 5e-5 m². Q = A v = 5e-5×12 = 6e-4 m³/s.

questions.question: Absolute pressure at 10 m depth in freshwater is closest to:
questions.explanation: Gauge ~1 atm at 10 m; add 1 atm atmospheric → about 2 atm absolute.

questions.question: A 0.040 m² door faces a 20 kPa pressure difference. Net force is:
For laminar flow, Reynolds number Re = ρ v D / μ. With ρ=1000 kg/m³, v=0.50 m/s, D=0.02 m, μ=1.0e-3 Pa·s, Re is:
A cube (0.20 m side) of density 500 kg/m³ floats in water. Fraction submerged is:
Pressure at bottom of 0.50 m of oil (ρ=800 kg/m³) over 1.0 m of water is:
questions.explanation: Oil column: 800·9.8·0.5 ≈ 3.9 kPa. Water column: 1000·9.8·1.0 ≈ 9.8 kPa. Total ≈ 13.7 kPa.

questions.question: An airplane wing has 12 kPa lower pressure on top over 20 m². Lift from pressure difference is:
A pipe reduces from 8 cm diameter to 4 cm. If flow is 20 L/s in the wide section, speed in the narrow section is:
steps: Multiply by 4 for the narrow section

questions.question: Water exits a 2.0 m tank bottom hole to the atmosphere. Ideal exit speed is:
questions.explanation: Torricelli: v = sqrt(2 g h) = sqrt(2·9.8·2) = sqrt(39.2) ≈ 6.3 m/s.
questions.fastStrategy: Use sqrt(2gh); ~6.3 m/s from 2 m head.

questions.question: Capillary rise h ≈ 2γ cosθ/(ρ g r). For water (γ=0.072 N/m, θ≈0) in a 0.50 mm radius tube, rise is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: 0.5 mm tube gives ~3 cm rise for water.

questions.question: A submerged balloon volume increases from 0.80 L at 3 atm to what at 1 atm (isothermal)?
questions.explanation: Boyle: P1V1 = P2V2 → V2 = 3 atm/1 atm ×0.80 = 2.4 L.
questions.fastStrategy: Inverse with pressure: 3× volume when pressure drops 3→1.

questions.question: Hydraulic press multiplies force by area ratio. With 10× larger output area, the ideal mechanical advantage is:
questions.explanation: Pascal: force scales with area. 10× larger area → 10× force (ideal).
questions.fastStrategy: Area ratio directly gives force ratio (lossless).

questions.question: Absolute pressure of 250 kPa corresponds to gauge pressure of:
Mass flow rate for water (ρ=1000) with volumetric flow 0.012 m³/s is:
A submerged block feels 250 N buoyant force. Displaced fluid volume is (ρ=1000):
questions.fastStrategy: Approx divide by 10,000 to get ~0.025 m³.

questions.question: Bernoulli assumes which condition is NOT required?
questions.explanation: Bernoulli requires steady, incompressible, non-viscous flow along a streamline; it does not assume turbulence (rather, laminar).

questions.question: A scuba diver breathes compressed air at 20 m depth (~3 atm). On rapid ascent with closed airway, lung volume could expand to:
questions.explanation: Boyle: V2 = V1·(P1/P2). P1≈3 atm, P2≈1 atm at surface → V2 ≈ 3× V1, risk of overexpansion.
questions.fastStrategy: Pressure drop 3→1 gives ~3× volume if trapped gas.
